learningObjective: Distinguish the control plane's authorization and version decisions from execution work and from the evidence plane's durable record of decisions and effects.
mediumRationale: A fitted vertical Mermaid trace follows the article's one logical credit through proposal, current authorization, durable pre-dispatch state, a lost response, and authoritative reconciliation. Plane names label the relevant decisions and observations instead of requiring a wide component catalogue. The lesson is relational rather than geometric.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Selected because the labelled vertical path and explicit no-dispatch branch reveal which plane authorizes, which performs the effect, and which observation establishes completion. The same logical call and downstream key remain visible without subgraph-driven width compression.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected because fixed coordinates add maintenance cost without teaching a quantitative, geometric, or shape-based relationship.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because a responsibility table can compare the planes but cannot show that control constrains the live path while evidence is emitted alongside it rather than after it.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because stepping through a fixed architecture adds controls and hidden state without changing the inference the reader must make.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the authoritative sources describe individual contracts rather than this article-specific synthesis. No source figure, layout, wording, or artwork is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the long article names many services and responsibilities; prose alone makes it easy to mistake the control, execution, and evidence planes for three independent inventories instead of one enforceable action path.

pages.insight: The instruction-tuning slide explains how models become responsive to instructions but provides no external authorization, execution, or evidence boundary.

The Toolformer slide defines a model that decides which API to call, when to call it, and which arguments to pass; it covers proposal behavior but not delegated authority, policy enforcement, durable execution, or audit evidence.
The neighboring LLM-data slide moves to pretraining corpora and scaling, adding no agent-platform mechanism.
The ML design-interview slide separates requirements, data, algorithms, evaluation, and experimentation, but does not identify shared platform planes.

The production-considerations slide asks about global launch, standard platforms, deployment paths, ownership, privacy, testing, monitoring, and rollback; it is the closest broad platform checklist but gives no enforced request path.
The neighboring system-design walkthrough covers requirements and data flow, not agent identity, authorization, tool effects, or evidence.
The next walkthrough slide connects model choice to offline and online experimentation but does not distinguish control from execution.
The project-setup slide covers goals, user experience, constraints, evaluation, personalization, and time to deployment without an agent governance boundary.
The data-pipeline slide covers storage, privacy, user-data care, and representation, which are neighboring governance concerns but not an action-control path.
The modeling slide discusses baselines, distributed training, and scale rather than runtime authority or side effects.
The serving slide covers model gating, monitoring, updates, inference placement, privacy, and interpretability, but not delegated authority or durable tool outcomes.

The adjacent Rules of Machine Learning slide emphasizes infrastructure, monitoring, policy layers, ownership, launch decisions, and training-serving skew; it provides operating context but no three-plane agent architecture.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed page by page for agents, Toolformer, tools, workflows, control planes, authorization, permissions, retries, idempotency, audit, observability, platforms, production, serving, deployment, and system design. Pages 104-106 and 161-169 were read as the two complete relevant neighborhoods. Page 105 stops at model-selected API calls, while pages 161-169 provide generic ML system and production checklists. No slide supplies the article's control/execution/evidence split, and no deck image, wording, values, or layout is reused.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
sources.usage: Used to verify the separation of policy decision and policy enforcement responsibilities, per-request access decisions, and least-privilege access rather than implicit trust.
sources.license: NIST states that employee-created works are generally not subject to U.S. copyright and grants broad reuse rights where it may hold foreign copyright, while warning that third-party material can differ. No NIST prose, figure, or layout is reused.

sources.title: RFC 8693: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
sources.usage: Used as the standards source for keeping the requesting actor's identity distinct from the subject on whose behalf it acts and for expressing bounded delegation in a token exchange.
sources.license: RFC 8693 is governed by the IETF Trust Legal Provisions. The implementation cites the delegation semantics only; it reproduces no RFC prose, diagram, code component, or layout.

sources.title: Temporal Workflow Execution overview
sources.usage: Used as official durable-execution documentation to verify persisted workflow state, event-history replay, and recovery after worker or infrastructure failure.
sources.license: No clear page-level grant for reusing documentation figures was identified. No Temporal prose, figure, product architecture, example, or visual arrangement is copied.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for Generative AI
sources.usage: Used as the official observability specification to verify that agent and model operations can emit portable spans, events, and metrics rather than treating a vendor runtime as the evidence contract.
sources.license: The repository is Apache-2.0 licensed, but the visual does not copy or adapt its schemas, prose, diagrams, or examples; the source is used only to validate the evidence-plane concept.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the boundary among the planes. The control plane determines which identities, versions, policies, and contracts may govern a call; the execution plane performs model, memory, and tool work under those decisions; the evidence plane durably records requests, decisions, attempts, and outcomes. The visual therefore avoids implying that the event store authorizes actions, that the model receives tool credentials, or that a control database should carry every sensitive payload.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected both relevant neighborhoods, then checked an IETF delegation standard and official NIST, Temporal, and OpenTelemetry sources before selecting an original three-plane boundary map.

implementation.accessibility: The Mermaid source provides an accessible title and a full text description. Direct CONTROL, EXECUTION, and EVIDENCE labels, an explicit HOLD branch, and repeated call/key identities carry the distinction without color. The fitted vertical trace passes native desktop, exact-390 phone, dark-theme, and print-style checks. These checks do not establish PDF pagination or learner comprehension.
